newsitem.title: UK: S&P says may cut Henkel ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P says may cut Henkel ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it placed its AA minus senior unsecured and A1 plus commercial paper ratings of Henkel KGaA's (Henkel) on CreditWatch with negative implications.
"About $160 million rated debt is affected," S&P said in a statement.
"The rating action follows Henkel's announcement that it is proposing to acquire the shares of Loctite Corp, which it does not already own.
"Henkel currently owns 35 percent of Loctite's shares, and estimates it will spend in the range of 1.7 billion marks for the acquisition of the remaining publicly held 65 percent," S&P said.
From a business perspective, the acquisition of Loctite, one of its largest competitors, would reinforce Henkel's global number one position in industrial and consumer adhesives, the agency said.

"Standard & Poor's considers these to be the strongest businesses of the Henkel group which is also engaged in consumer products and chemicals. The acquisition of a U.S. company would also improve its geographical sales split, which currently is biased towards Europe (80 percent of sales)."

But a 1.7 billion mark acquisition, if debt-financed, would double Henkel's debt, and S&P estimated operating profit net interest coverage could deteriorate from around five times in 1995 to three times next year on a proforma basis in 1997.

S&P said it will meet with Henkel's management within the next few weeks to discuss the financing of the acquisition including the potential for disposals of non-core assets as well for an equity issue.
